project.title: RASA AI — Audition Intelligence & Casting Support
project.short_description: An AI-assisted audition review workspace that brings screenplay context, role requirements, visual and vocal audition observations, reviewer notes, audition comparison, and audition-record retrieval into one workflow. RASA AI supports evidence-informed human casting decisions; it does not make casting decisions.
project.category: AI / Computer Vision / Audio Analysis / NLP / Casting Support

features_used: Manual audition-record upsert using SQL MERGE keyed by AUDITION_ID
Audition payload storage as JSON in a CLOB with summary fields
Retrieval of recent audition records and JSON payload decoding

confirmed: Db2 connectivity in the project environment

ibm_db2.persistence_note: The local JSON audition library remains the source of truth. Db2 synchronization is manual and does not automatically replace the local JSON storage workflow.

technologies: Timestamp-based visual and vocal evidence alignment

retrieval.storage: In-memory document store rebuilt for each search operation
retrieval.note: BM25 scores indicate keyword relevance, not acting quality or role suitability.

application_workflow: Screenplay/story text input or text-based PDF extraction
Rule-based candidate character-cue and scene-heading identification
Reviewer-defined role requirements and audition prompts
Video analysis using OpenCV and MediaPipe landmarks
Timestamp-based combined visual and vocal evidence timeline
Local audition library with reviewer notes, status, shortlist markers, comparison, and export
Haystack BM25 search over saved audition records
IBM Db2 connection, table initialization, manual synchronization, and read-back
decision_support_notice: RASA AI does not make casting decisions. Computer-vision measurements, optional facial-expression labels, vocal features, rule-based screenplay cues, and retrieval scores are signals for human review, not validated measures of acting quality, personality, internal emotion, diagnosis, or role suitability. Qualified human reviewers remain responsible for casting decisions.
